top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye is a genuine invention: the magic-wavelength lattice cancels the light shifts of the clock levels so that thousands of neutral atoms are interrogated free of Doppler and recoil shifts, which neither the 2005 comb prize nor the 2012 single-quantum-system prize covers. It is experimentally mature, with independent clocks at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE agreeing at the 10^-18 level, it already serves as a measuring instrument for redshift and constants, and the two-name allocation is clean. Awarding nothing would withhold a reproduced, well-scoped achievement.
recusal_note: Possible lineage connection only: I spent a year during my PhD in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, the precision-spectroscopy tradition of Jun Ye's JILA group; no collaboration, co-authorship or financial tie with Katori or Ye, so no recusal need apparent. Also WACQT and Deep Light Vision AB roles, unrelated to this slate.
